tags.gist: Thanks FDA and argues the key question is who answers for acting on an output, since accuracy belongs to models and accountability to people.
Endorses the two axes but wants a named accountable human reviewer and reversibility made first-class variables that move a device down the risk surface.
Wants the clinician-facing lower-risk class tied explicitly to the section 520(o)(1)(E) independent-review criterion as a name-the-human design target.
Wants the model benchmarked alone but clinical confirmation to score the deployed human-AI team, with the human's role being accountability rather than accuracy.
Says shared postmarket responsibility functions only with a portable, tamper-evident, PHI-free record of who reviewed each output and what they decided.
Would anchor agentic oversight to whether a named licensed human reviews and signs each consequential or hard-to-reverse action, not to autonomy labels.
Calls the principle that a master file is no device approval and the deploying sponsor stays responsible exactly right.
Would keep the path light for retrieval, drafting and triage, reserving the accountable licensed human for consequential clinical or coverage decisions.
A physician who runs attestation software supports the paper's central instincts and offers five refinements from systems in use.
Urges the framework to keep model accuracy and personal accountability separate and to build around the second.
Wants the framework to state that routing consequential outputs through an accountable reviewer lowers effective risk, with reversibility treated the same way.
Wants devices whose basis a professional can independently review before acting named as a distinct lower-risk class under section 520(o)(1)(E).
Cites evidence that adding a reviewer does not reliably raise accuracy; wants confirmation to measure the team as deployed while the model is benchmarked alone.
Calls the escalation, calibration and clinical-deferral competencies exactly right, since knowing when to hand off is the safety behavior.
Offers a pattern of signed, timestamped, PHI-free attestations anchored to a tamper-evident ledger so human sign-offs can be verified afterward.
Proposes a functional test at each consequential action, whether a qualified human examines the basis and answers for it, as more robust than autonomy levels.
Wants FDA to keep central that a master file is not an approval and the deploying party plus the signing clinician hold accountability.
Sums up: name the accountable human as risk-lowering element, regulatory class, unit of confirmation, postmarket record and agentic checkpoint.
